text: Thanks — I can reproduce the intent: a flag declared `required=True` should error out when omitted. I've started a fix and will confirm once the test suite passes.
Got it — `click.echo` (and the progress bar / pager) should no-op instead of crashing when there is no console stream attached (pythonw.exe). I'm on it; I'll confirm when the suite is green.
Right — for a `flag_value` option, a set envvar should just switch the flag on (yielding the configured `flag_value`), not be used verbatim as the value. Fixing that now.
Understood — a `click.argument(...)`/`click.option(...)` decorator should be reusable across commands (each application should build a fresh parameter with the given `cls`). Fixing that now.
Got it — `resolve_path=True` must resolve a relative symlink target against the link's own directory (so `/tmp/demo/link` -> `/tmp/demo/real.txt`). Fixing that now.
Right — the help text for a boolean flag should reflect the effective default (including `default_map`), not just the flag's own `default`. Fixing that now.

Fixed. Root cause: `Option.__init__` unconditionally set `self.default = False` for flags when no `default=` was given, so a required flag always looked "supplied" and the `required` check was dead code. Now the flag default is only forced when the option is not required, so an omitted required flag raises `MissingParameter` (exit 2). The error hint also now lists both spellings: `Error: Missing option '--on' / '--off'.` Verified: no args -> error; `--on` -> True; `--off` -> False; plain `--flag` required -> error; explicit `default=` and non-required flags unchanged. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Fixed. The default-stream helpers now return `None` when `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` is `None` (pythonw.exe), and `echo` returns early instead of calling `.write` on `None`; `pager`/`ProgressBar` no longer crash either (the bar falls back to an in-memory sink). Verified with both streams set to `None`: `click.echo`, `echo(..., err=True)`, `echo(..., nl=False)`, `echo(bytes)`, `echo_via_pager` and `progressbar` all complete without raising, and normal output to real streams is unchanged. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Fixed. `Option.value_from_envvar` was returning the raw env text for every option; for a flag with a custom `flag_value` the env var now just switches the flag on and yields the configured `flag_value`. `UPPER=whatever cmd` and `UPPER=1 cmd` both print `upper`; unset/empty env still falls back to the default; `--upper` on the command line is unchanged. Boolean flags (`--on/--off`, `is_flag=True`) still convert the env string to a bool (`SHOUT=' true '` -> True, `SHOUT=0` -> False), and `multiple`/`nargs` env splitting is untouched. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Fixed. `click.argument`'s decorator did `attrs.pop("cls", Argument)` directly on the dict shared by the closure, so the first application permanently removed `cls` and later ones fell back to plain `Argument`. It now copies `attrs` first (the same fix `click.option` already had), so a decorator built once can be reused: both commands now get your `MyArgument`. Reused `click.option(..., cls=...)` and single-use decorators are unaffected. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Fixed. `Path.convert` was doing `os.readlink(rv)` and then `os.path.realpath` on the bare link target, so a relative target (`link -> real.txt`) got resolved against your current working directory. It now resolves the link in place (via `pathlib.Path.resolve()`), so `/tmp/demo5/link` -> `/tmp/demo5/real.txt` regardless of cwd. Absolute targets, symlink chains, bytes/pathlib inputs, `resolve_path=False` and the `exists`/`file_okay`/`dir_okay` checks all behave as before. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Fixed. The boolean-flag branch of `Option.get_help_record` chose the displayed opt name from the raw `self.default` attribute instead of the effective default, ignoring `ctx.default_map`. It now uses the value from `get_default(ctx)` (which consults the default map), so with `default_map={'foo': {'name': True}}` the help shows `[default: name]` while the runtime value stays `True`. With the map absent or set to False it still shows `[default: no-name]`, and single-opt bool flags / `show_default="..."` are unchanged. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.
